safety-rails effort (my own just-merged PR #4 — 98 files, ~9,500 lines) plus
an earlier Software Factory / opportunity-research merge and the `trillion`

- `.env.example`, `AGENT.md`, `README.md`, `agent/config.py`,

- `.gitignore`, `tests/test_analytics_tool.py` — changed on both sides but
  auto-merged cleanly per `git merge-tree` (`merged` / `result` lines, no
  further hunk shown).
- `docs/superpowers/specs/...design.md`, `tests/test_serve_chat_sessions.py`,
  `tests/test_serve_software_factory_wiring.py` — added only on PR #3's
  side (`added in remote`), should apply with zero conflict.

**Diff size of the three highest-risk files, main vs. the merge-base** (i.e.
how much main moved under PR #3's feet):
```
agent/tools/project_fs.py |  11 ++          (small — likely low real risk)
agent/config.py           | 125 ++          (new Settings fields, likely appends)
serve.py                  | 198 ++++++--     (large — P1/P5/P6/P7 all touched serve.py)
```
`serve.py` is the one I'd bet on being the actual hard conflict — it's
where the confirmation gate, notes/email tools, heartbeat endpoints, and
security-shield endpoint all got wired into `build_app()` on main's side,
while PR #3 independently touched it for chat-session / Software-Factory
wiring review fixes.

## Why this matters for whoever resolves it

`agent/tools/project_fs.py` and `agent/tools/analytics_tool.py` on **main**
have since been touched by this session's own P1 safety-rails work (adding
`risk` / `requires_confirmation` fields at the `BaseTool` level — see
`agent/tools/base.py`). PR #3's changes to those same two files are a
*different* independent hardening effort (bubblewrap sandboxing, a
SQL-literal-exclusion regex fix) that predates and doesn't know about the
safety-rails work. These are almost certainly complementary, not
contradictory — but whoever resolves the conflict needs to verify that by
reading both sides, not just pick one side mechanically.
